summary.prose: This Story gives every stored artifact one shape and one reader and writer. An Artifact carries an identity from the s1 id module, a description, an optional parent, references, the lifecycle and tracker binding shapes the HLD already approved (declared here unchanged, with their behaviour left to s3 and s6), attachments and its own payload. One synchronous decoder reads a head; ArtifactStore.read wraps it, readWithHistory adds the change log and feedback, and the old Define, HLD, LLD and Plan readers delegate to it. A write prepares the head so the authoritative revision and a recoverable operation id are known, stages it in a required write journal, records it in the change log, then replaces the head. A repository version marker lets the new tools refuse an unconverted repository.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Chosen framework (a1): a shared artifact envelope with typed payloads, stored as a head file plus two append-only sidecar files whose lines carry the owning artifact id, behind a single identity module, with one upfront conversion and no compatibility code. The envelope carries identity, description, parent, references, a typed lifecycle (revision, approval, review, signoffs, staleness, status) and a tracker binding or attachments; the change log and feedback are separate append-only line files; each existing artifact type shrinks to a payload codec and a renderer. Tracker comment reading and attaching are added to the port and implemented for the GitHub adapter only.

ownedContracts.name: ArtifactEnvelope
ownedContracts.purpose: The common shape of every stored entity and the one reader and writer for it, with References and namespaced Actors.

ownedContracts.name: HistoryRecords
ownedContracts.purpose: The change log entry and the Feedback entry shapes, the persisted sidecar record that carries the owning artifact id, and the append and read API, including how an update says which feedback it addressed.

ownedContracts.name: RepoSchemaVersion
ownedContracts.purpose: The repository-level marker that records whether a repository has been converted, so the conversion is repeatable and the new tools refuse an unconverted repository.
ownedContracts.interfaceSketch:
interface RepoSchema { version: number; convertedAt?: string }
interface RepoSchemaGate { read(repo: string): RepoSchema; require(repo: string, atLeast: number): { ok: true } | { ok: false; message: string } }

consumedContracts.name: ArtifactIdScheme
consumedContracts.purpose: The single place artifact ids are made and recognised: the existing hierarchical typed ids extended for Epic, Story, Task, the Tasks file and diagrams, one story and task form, the folder-name date source, and the functional-requirement id helpers that live in id.ts today.

boundary.internal: The envelope model, the one reader and writer, the History API and the sidecar record shape as a contract, and the repository version marker. Private to this Story are the head-file schema, the per-type payload codec registry and how the old per-type read functions delegate to the reader.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: The id module and its removal of the second scheme: the folder-name formatter moved into the path scheme, the date source fixed to the epic's creation time, the functional-requirement id helpers and their callers moved with stored FR ids staying valid, issue titles switched to the artifact id, and the delivery module's ordinals. The old issue-body marker is not read. Private to this Story are the exact text of the issue title and the relocation of the helpers.

The lifecycle rules: status transitions, the revision and content-hash computation, the staleness record, the completion roll-up and the integrity check against the log tail on approve, review and complete. Private to this Story are the hash canonicalisation and how a roll-up is cached or recomputed.

The physical sidecar storage: file layout, the merge attributes for the line files, per-artifact filtering, read-time ordering and de-duplication, and the write order of log entry before head with the repair of a log that is ahead of its head. Private to this Story are the line format and the file naming beside a head.

People-facing feedback: adding feedback and replies from a client, listing open feedback, the addresses rule at revision time, and the per-user identity declaration with alias linking. Private to this Story are the identity file format and the display of linked identities.

The typed binding and attachments, the tracker port additions implemented for GitHub, the retry of pending links and posts, and the switch of unit-issue bookkeeping to the binding. Private to this Story are the permalink construction and the retry bookkeeping.

Task artifacts: creation of the Tasks file and the Task issues at plan approval, direct edits of a Task's own content with local re-approval, refusal of structural edits, and the re-plan reconciliation. Private to this Story are the diff of a Task against the new plan and the build-round recording in a Task's history.

Comment sync: reading human comments into feedback at implement, validate or on request, classifying a revision request or a suggestion from the first line, and posting feedback once. Private to this Story are the first-line commands, the derived since point and the filter for the framework's own posts.

The conversion command: previews, repeats, back-fills history, renames standalone S001 to s1 rewriting the references it can with no alias, creates Epic, Story and Task artifacts for what exists, verifies through the delivery reader, and sets the repository version. Private to this Story are the per-type conversion mappings and the verification report.

hldContextSlice.rolloutPhase: Phase A — identity and the common model

nonFunctional.performance: Reading an artifact reads its head; the log tail is read only on approve, review and complete, and counts, open feedback and status are computed on read. The delivery loader still reads each artifact once. Loading a repository of about a thousand artifacts must stay within twice today's load time on the same machine.
nonFunctional.security: Gates use the live tracker identity only; declared aliases are never trusted for a decision. The identity file is local and read for attribution. Tracker comments are read through the existing gh path of the GitHub adapter, with no new credential and no direct REST call.
nonFunctional.observability: Every state change appends a change log entry with actor, operation and, where relevant, revision and status; a conflict, a log-ahead-of-head repair, a failed attach and a pending link are logged and surfaced in the unit's result, not hidden.
nonFunctional.durability: Heads are replaced atomically as today; sidecar lines are append-only and de-duplicated by (artifactId, entry id) so a repeated append is harmless; a write appends its log entry before it replaces the head so a failure between the two leaves a detectable, repairable gap; the conversion is one commit, repeatable, and reverts with one git revert.

api.name: ArtifactStore.write

parameters.name: a
parameters.purpose: The whole envelope to store. Its lifecycle is persisted as supplied except lifecycle.revision.number, which the store sets from the prepared write; transitions and the content hash are s3's.

parameters.name: by
parameters.purpose: The actor recorded on the change log entry.

returns.meaning: Resolves once the head is replaced; a failure to clear the journal afterwards is logged and does not fail the write.

errors.condition: a.id is not a valid artifact id
no codec for the kind
the codec rejects the payload, the parent is not an artifact id matching ArtifactIds.parentOf, or a reference whose type is an artifact type names an invalid artifact id

preconditions: by is an Actor with a namespaced non-empty id
the store was built with a WriteJournal (only the explicitly non-durable test constructor omits it)
postconditions: any pending operation the journal reports for this id is completed first: if the head already equals the staged bytes the journal is only cleared, otherwise the staged bytes are written under the SAME operation id; only then is the new write accepted
the head is prepared by the pure prepareArtifactWrite, so the revision and the exact bytes are known before any file changes

the kind is content when the payload (body or citations) or the description changed, and meta-only when only references, parent, attachments, binding or lifecycle changed, so only a content change moves the revision (k3)

the operation id is a hash of the artifact id, the prior revision number and the prepared bytes; the journal records { operationId, priorRevision, bytes } so a retry reuses it even after the head moved on
the order is stage in the journal, append the change log entry with that id and the authoritative revision, replace the head, clear the journal
meta.lifecycle.revision.number and the log entry's revision carry the number the prepare step returned
the merged meta keeps the prior head's meta and replaces only meta.envelope, meta.lifecycle and meta.revision; on create the kind's codec supplies the identity meta
children are not stored on the parent

dataModelChanges.details: The envelope: { id, description, parent?, references, lifecycle, binding?, attachments, payload }. Stored in the head under meta.envelope (description, parent, references, binding, attachments) and meta.lifecycle, beside the existing identity and anchor meta; the payload is body plus citations. The outer { meta, body, citations } shape is kept so writeArtifact and every raw reader keep working. Kind-specific payload shapes stay in src/workflow/artifacts and are reached through the codec registry.
dataModelChanges.schemaDiff: meta.envelope = { description: string; parent?: Reference; references: Reference[]; binding?: TrackerBinding; attachments: Attachment[] }; meta.lifecycle = Lifecycle

dataModelChanges.details: A pure synchronous function decodeArtifactHead(id, raw) in src/workflow/artifact-core that parses the head text, selects the codec by the kind ArtifactIds.parse returns, and returns the Artifact plus the parsed head. ArtifactStore.read is an asynchronous wrapper over it and the four gates readers call it, so there is one decoder. A head with no meta.envelope or meta.lifecycle decodes with empty parts.

dataModelChanges.entity: Lifecycle family (Status, Revision, Approval, Review, Signoff, Staleness, Lifecycle)
dataModelChanges.details: Declared in src/workflow/artifact-core/types.ts exactly as HLD sc4 (owned by s3) defines them: Status draft | pending-review | approved | in-signoff | changes-requested | signed-off | rejected | completed | withdrawn | superseded; Revision { number, contentHash, at, by }; Approval { revision, by, at, override? }; Review { revision, reviewer, party, verdict, counts, at, report? }; Signoff { revision, request, state, actors, at }; Staleness { upstream, upstreamRevision, since }; Lifecycle { status, revision, approval?, review?, signoffs, stale? }. s2 stores and reads the shape; transitions, the content hash and the roll-up are s3's. An empty lifecycle is { status: draft, revision: { number: 0, contentHash: '', at: '', by: <system actor> }, signoffs: [] }.

Declared exactly as HLD sc6 (owned by s6) defines them: TrackerBinding { reference, createdAtRevision, posted[], pendingLink? } and Attachment { target, revision, at, externalId? }. s2 validates only that references are well formed; their behaviour is s6's. A tracker issue is never an artifact (k6): the binding points at it.

Actor { id, kind, name?, properties } with a namespaced lower-case id (github:alice, insrc:daemon); Reference { entityId, type, relation, fragment?, quote? } where type is the target's type and relation says why the link exists. entityId is an artifact id or an external id (owner/repo#N, a code path, a URL) with a namespaced type, as Gap 7 allows; ArtifactIds.parse checks it only when type is an artifact type. The parent is a Reference with relation derived-from whose entityId must be an artifact id equal to ArtifactIds.parentOf of the artifact's own key, so the Epic, Story and Task chain is given by each artifact's parent (ac6).

As in HLD sc3: { id, actor, timestamp, operation, revision?, status?, outcome?, references?, addresses? } with the seventeen operations. It is a new type in src/workflow/artifact-core/types.ts and is distinct from the build file-change entry.

The existing provenance ChangeLogEntry { target, summary?, author, timestamp } and ChangeLog are used by the BUILD record's file-level change log, so they are kept and renamed FileChangeEntry and FileChangeLog to avoid a clash with the artifact operation log. Consumers are updated: collectBuildChangeLog, StandaloneBuildRecord.body.changeLog and changeLogBodyLines. Stored data is unchanged because only the TypeScript names move.
dataModelChanges.schemaDiff: ChangeLogEntry -> FileChangeEntry; ChangeLog -> FileChangeLog (type names only)

dataModelChanges.details: { id, text, actor, timestamp, feedback (replies), kind: comment | suggestion | revision-request, anchor?, revision?, source?, batchId? }. The anchor is { quote?, prefix?, suffix?, section?, lines? } (binding requirement 5): prefix and suffix are kept, limits stay 500 for the quote and 40 for prefix and suffix, section carries the nearest heading slug. A pure function converts a stored FeedbackEntry for s9: comment becomes text; author becomes Actor { id: unknown:<author>, kind: person, properties: {} } because the legacy string has no namespace; an absent kind becomes comment, feedback and comment become comment, suggestion stays suggestion; quote, prefix and suffix copy across; sectionSlug becomes section with the same value; target.segment becomes anchor.lines; target.version, when it is an integer revision, becomes revision, and any other value is reported in the conversion result as unmapped rather than dropped; target.file is dropped when it is the owning artifact's own document and reported otherwise; batchId copies; decision is not a Feedback field and becomes the approve, reject or feedback outcome of the change log entry of that batch.
dataModelChanges.schemaDiff: FeedbackAnchor.sectionSlug -> Feedback.anchor.section; FeedbackEntry.comment -> Feedback.text; FeedbackEntry.kind (optional) -> Feedback.kind (required, default comment)

dataModelChanges.details: A pure function in src/workflow/storage.ts that takes the same inputs as writeArtifact and returns { bytes, revision, changed } without touching the file system except to read the prior head. writeArtifact is rewritten as prepare then writeAtomic, so the revision rule has one implementation.

{ stage(id, op: { operationId, priorRevision, bytes }): Promise<void>; pending(id): Promise<{ operationId, priorRevision, bytes } | undefined>; clear(id, operationId): Promise<void> }. The store requires one; s2 ships an in-memory implementation for tests and for an explicitly named non-durable constructor, and s4 implements the durable pending-head file and the start-up recovery. pending lets a retry find the staged operation and reuse its operation id and bytes, including after the head was already replaced.

Each kind registers a codec { decode(head), encode(payload, ctx) } over the { meta, body, citations } head. encode returns { meta, body, citations }; on create the codec builds the kind's identity meta from ctx (epicHash, epicSlug, createdAt, epicCreatedAt obtained through the s1 stampRootAnchor and resolveEpicAnchor helpers, standalone, sizeClass and the other fields the existing readers use), and on update the prior head's meta is kept. The store merges the prior meta first and replaces only meta.envelope, meta.lifecycle and meta.revision, so workItemAnchorCreatedAt and the path and renderer code keep reading the same fields. The AMD codec requires the converted head and refuses a flat amendment with a pointer to the s9 conversion.

{ artifactId, entry } is one line of a sidecar file. s2 provides appendSidecarLine(path, record), the one function that appends a JSON line with appendFileSync to the path it is given, and an in-memory reader and appender for tests. Which path, the line format beyond a JSON object per line, ordering, de-duplication and repair are s4's through sc5's SidecarStore.
{ version: number; convertedAt?: string } stored in .insrc/schema.json. Absent means version 1 (unconverted). The version s9 sets is 2. s2 only reads and requires; s9 writes.

WRITER_NAMES gains appendFileSync and appendSidecarLine, and a store-write rule is added. The detector keeps recognising the existing five writers exactly as before (invariant from bundle 4). Negative controls cover a raw, an aliased, a renamed, a namespace and an injected appendFileSync, and a store write with no entry. The store file's inventory entry is added in the same task as the store file, because the inventory test rejects an entry whose file does not exist.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: Implements the Artifact types, ArtifactStore (read, write, childrenOf), the shared decoder and codec registry and the head layout; the head is written through the unchanged writeArtifact rule via the pure prepare step. readWithHistory is recorded by the sc2 methodAdd amendment already filed.

Implements the ChangeLogEntry, Feedback and SidecarRecord shapes, the History API and the append primitive. The anchor keeps prefix and suffix; section replaces sectionSlug with the stated conversion.
Implements RepoSchemaGate.read and require over .insrc/schema.json; s9 sets and checks the version.
Uses ArtifactIds.parse for every id the store receives and ArtifactIds.parentOf for the parent reference; adds no id rule.
Declares the Lifecycle family exactly as sc4 defines it and stores it; the rules that move it are s3's.
Declares TrackerBinding and Attachment exactly as sc6 defines them and stores them; their behaviour is s6's.

errorCases.scenario: The head file is not valid JSON, or has no meta or body object
errorCases.detection: The shared decoder parses the text and checks that meta and body are plain objects; a parse error or a failed check raises ArtifactShapeError naming the id and path
errorCases.response: Throw ArtifactShapeError from ArtifactStore.read or from the delegating Define, HLD, LLD or Plan reader; no part is guessed and nothing is written
errorCases.userImpact: The artifact cannot be read until the file is repaired by hand; other artifacts are unaffected

errorCases.scenario: An unconverted amendment (a flat AMD file with no meta and body) is read through the store
errorCases.detection: The AMD codec finds no meta object in the parsed file
errorCases.response: Throw ArtifactShapeError whose message names the s9 amendment conversion; childrenOf skips it and logs
errorCases.userImpact: Amendments cannot be read through the store until s9 converts them; the existing amendment commands are unaffected until then

errorCases.scenario: A read or write names an id the s1 module does not accept, for example LLD-<h16>-S001
errorCases.detection: ArtifactIds.parse returns undefined for the id
errorCases.response: Throw InvalidArtifactKeyError; the message points to the s9 conversion for an upper-case story
errorCases.userImpact: Old upper-case artifacts fail until the conversion runs

errorCases.scenario: No head exists for the id on read
errorCases.detection: existsSync on the head path is false
errorCases.response: Throw ArtifactNotFoundError for the store, or ArtifactMissingError for the gates readers, as today
errorCases.userImpact: A caller that expected the artifact sees a clear not-found error

errorCases.scenario: A kind has no registered payload codec
errorCases.detection: The codec registry lookup by ArtifactIds.parse(id).kind finds nothing
errorCases.response: Throw UnknownArtifactKindError; the store never passes a payload through untyped
errorCases.userImpact: A new artifact kind cannot be stored until its codec is registered

errorCases.scenario: The parent is not an artifact id, or differs from ArtifactIds.parentOf of the artifact's own key, or a reference whose type is an artifact type names an invalid artifact id
errorCases.detection: ArtifactStore.write checks the parent with ArtifactIds.parse and parentOf, and checks each reference's entityId with ArtifactIds.parse only when its type is an artifact type
errorCases.response: Throw ArtifactShapeError naming the reference; an external reference (owner/repo#N, a code path, a URL) is accepted without a check
errorCases.userImpact: A malformed parent or artifact link is refused before anything is written; valid tracker and code references are never blocked

errorCases.scenario: Preparing the head fails (unreadable prior head, a codec rejecting the payload)
errorCases.detection: prepareArtifactWrite throws before any file is touched
errorCases.response: Throw the error; no journal entry, no log line and no head change exist
errorCases.userImpact: The write fails cleanly with nothing to repair

errorCases.scenario: Staging the prepared head in the WriteJournal fails
errorCases.response: Rethrow before the log append, so nothing is logged and the head is unchanged
errorCases.userImpact: The write fails visibly and can be retried

errorCases.scenario: The log append fails after the head was staged
errorCases.detection: appendSidecarLine or History.appendLog throws (disk full, permission)
errorCases.response: Rethrow; the staged operation stays in the journal and the head file is unchanged; the next write for this id finds it through pending and completes it under the same operation id
errorCases.userImpact: The write is reported failed; a retry reuses the staged operation id

errorCases.scenario: The head replace fails or the process stops after the log append
errorCases.detection: writeAtomic throws, or WriteJournal.pending still reports the operation at the next write or start
errorCases.response: Rethrow and log the artifact id and operation id at warn; the next write replays the staged bytes under the same operation id, which readers de-duplicate
errorCases.userImpact: The log never names a revision the head cannot reach, and no second entry is made for the same write

errorCases.scenario: The head was replaced but clearing the journal failed
errorCases.response: Log the failure at warn and let the write succeed; the next write finds the pending operation, sees the head already equals the staged bytes and only clears it, reusing the staged operation id
errorCases.userImpact: The caller sees success; the leftover journal entry is cleaned on the next write

errorCases.scenario: A write is made while a different operation is pending for the same id
errorCases.detection: WriteJournal.pending returns an operation whose bytes are neither the current head nor the new write
errorCases.response: Complete the pending operation first, then run the new write against the resulting head
errorCases.userImpact: Unrelated writes cannot overtake a staged one, so the log stays in order

errorCases.scenario: A feedback entry has an empty text, an unknown kind or an anchor over its limits
errorCases.detection: History.appendFeedback validates the entry before the append
errorCases.response: Throw HistoryEntryError naming the field; nothing is appended
errorCases.userImpact: The caller learns exactly what to fix

errorCases.scenario: A sidecar line is not a valid SidecarRecord when read
errorCases.detection: The reader port or History.log fails to parse a line or finds a missing artifactId or entry

A content write carries the whole prior meta.tracker block; the envelope's binding does not drop meta.tracker
workItemAnchorCreatedAt requires meta.epicCreatedAt, so a store write keeps the head's identity meta and never drops it
The head keeps the { meta, body, citations } outer shape and is replaced atomically with writeAtomic
The Lifecycle, TrackerBinding and Attachment shapes are exactly the ones HLD sc4 and sc6 define, and a Reference may name an artifact or an external id
The build change log keeps its stored shape: only the TypeScript names of ChangeLogEntry and ChangeLog move
Feedback quote is at most 500 characters and prefix and suffix at most 40, and the anchor keeps its prefix and suffix
The detector recognises writeArtifact, writeRecordFile, writeAtomic, writeFileSync and renameSync exactly as before, and every writer file has an inventory entry
Amendment files keep their flat stored shape until the s9 conversion
readDefineArtifact, readHldArtifact, readLldArtifact and readPlanArtifact stay synchronous and keep their return shapes and missing-file errors
Artifact ids are the strict s1 form and the parent chain comes from ArtifactIds.parentOf; the delivery loader reads each artifact once

migration.stateBefore: Each artifact type keeps cross-cutting facts as loose optional meta fields and its feedback inside body.feedback. writeArtifact builds and writes the head in one function and returns the revision only after the write. gates.ts readDefineArtifact, readHldArtifact, readLldArtifact and readPlanArtifact each parse the head JSON themselves and are synchronous. The write inventory recognises five writers and several existing files call appendFileSync unseen. The build change log uses ChangeLogEntry and ChangeLog from the provenance types. Amendments are flat files. (bundles c1 to c6)
migration.stateAfter: src/workflow/artifact-core holds the envelope types (including the sc4 and sc6 shapes unchanged), the shared synchronous decoder, the codec registry, ArtifactStore with readWithHistory and a required WriteJournal, History, appendSidecarLine and RepoSchemaGate. storage.ts has a pure prepareArtifactWrite and writeArtifact is prepare then write. The four gates readers delegate to the shared decoder and stay synchronous. The build change log types are renamed FileChangeEntry and FileChangeLog. The inventory detector knows appendFileSync, appendSidecarLine and the store write, with negative controls, and every file it newly flags has an entry. No stored data is converted: s3 to s8 build on the store and s9 converts, including amendments.

migrationSteps.action: Add src/workflow/artifact-core/types.ts declaring the envelope, Actor, Reference, ChangeLogEntry, Feedback, SidecarRecord, RepoSchema, the errors, and the sc4 Lifecycle family and sc6 TrackerBinding and Attachment exactly as the HLD defines them. Rename the provenance ChangeLogEntry and ChangeLog to FileChangeEntry and FileChangeLog and update collectBuildChangeLog, StandaloneBuildRecord and changeLogBodyLines. Stored data does not change.

Split writeArtifact in src/workflow/storage.ts into a pure prepareArtifactWrite returning the bytes, the revision and whether content changed, and a writeArtifact that calls it and then writeAtomic. Its signature and results stay identical; the existing writeArtifact tests must pass unchanged.

Add src/workflow/artifact-core/sidecar.ts with appendSidecarLine and the in-memory reader and appender, and src/workflow/artifact-core/history.ts implementing History with entry validation including the anchor limits. In the same change extend the inventory detector for appendFileSync and appendSidecarLine, add the negative controls, give an inventory entry to the sidecar file, and add entries for every existing file the detector newly flags (src/daemon/fatal.ts, src/daemon/shutdown.ts, the analyze-step, build-step, workflow-step and review-step handlers, src/config/feedback.ts, and the appendRunLog call in src/workflow/storage.ts). The inventory test must pass at the end of this step.

Add the kind codec registry and a codec for each existing kind except AMD, each owning encode(payload, ctx) and the kind's identity meta, plus the pure synchronous decodeArtifactHead. The AMD codec requires the converted head and throws a pointer to the s9 conversion for a flat amendment.

Delegate readDefineArtifact, readHldArtifact, readLldArtifact and readPlanArtifact in src/workflow/gates.ts to decodeArtifactHead. They stay synchronous, keep their return shapes and their missing-file errors, and a head without envelope parts decodes with empty parts, so the delegation is safe before the conversion. The existing gates tests must pass unchanged.

Add src/workflow/artifact-core/store.ts with ArtifactStore (read, readWithHistory, write, childrenOf) and the WriteJournal port with pending, using prepareArtifactWrite, the codecs and History in the order: complete any pending operation, stage, append log, replace head, clear. Extend the inventory detector with the store-write rule and add the store file's inventory entry in this same step, since the inventory test rejects an entry for a file that does not exist.
Add RepoSchemaGate over .insrc/schema.json: read (absent means version 1) and require.
Add the pure legacy feedback conversion with its report of unmapped fields so s9 can run it.

Record for s9 in docs/plans/core-data-model.md: convert every flat amendment to the enveloped head; add meta.envelope and meta.lifecycle to every head (moving approvedAt, rejectedAt, rejectReason, review, reviewOverride, reviewResolutions and the staleness comparisons into the lifecycle and tracker into the binding); turn body.feedback entries into sidecar feedback lines through step 8; set the repository marker to version 2. None of this runs in this Story.

migration.backwardCompat: None is kept, by the owner's ruling. The changes to existing modules are internal: writeArtifact is split with identical behaviour, the four gates readers delegate to the shared decoder with unchanged return shapes and errors, the build change log types are renamed (type names only, stored data unchanged), and the detector gains writers. The store and ports are additive. A repository that has not been converted reads as schema version 1 and the new tools refuse it through RepoSchemaGate.require, and an unconverted amendment is refused by the store with a pointer to s9 while the existing amendment commands keep working.

alternativesConsidered.name: Store with a required journal, a recoverable operation id, a shared synchronous decoder and codec-owned metadata
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: ArtifactStore over a pure prepare step with a REQUIRED WriteJournal whose pending(id) lets a retry reuse the staged operation id; one synchronous decodeArtifactHead that the async read and the gates readers share; codecs own the kind's identity meta; sc4 and sc6 shapes declared unchanged.
alternativesConsidered.approach: New module group src/workflow/artifact-core. types.ts declares the envelope, Actor, Reference, ChangeLogEntry, Feedback, SidecarRecord, RepoSchema and, unchanged from the HLD, the sc4 Lifecycle family and the sc6 TrackerBinding and Attachment. storage.ts splits writeArtifact into a pure prepareArtifactWrite and writeArtifact calls it then writeAtomic. decodeArtifactHead(id, raw) is a pure synchronous decoder over the { meta, body, citations } head; ArtifactStore.read and readWithHistory wrap it, and readDefineArtifact, readHldArtifact, readLldArtifact and readPlanArtifact in gates.ts call it and keep returning the stored artifact in their current shapes, so no caller becomes asynchronous; a head with no envelope parts decodes with empty parts, so this is safe before the conversion. ArtifactStore is built with a required WriteJournal (a journal-free store exists only through an explicitly named non-durable test constructor). write(): first completes any pending operation the journal reports for the id (head already equal to the staged bytes: clear only; otherwise replay the staged bytes under the SAME operation id); then chooses the kind (content when the payload or the description changed, meta-only otherwise), prepares the head, derives the operation id from the artifact id, the prior revision and the prepared bytes, stages { operationId, priorRevision, bytes } in the journal, appends the change log entry with that id and the authoritative revision, replaces the head, and clears the journal; a clear failure after a successful replace is logged and does not fail the write. Each kind's codec owns encode(payload, ctx) and supplies the kind's identity meta from ctx on create (epicHash, epicSlug, epicCreatedAt through the s1 anchor helpers, createdAt, standalone and the other fields existing readers use) and takes it from the prior head on update; the store merges the prior meta first and replaces only meta.envelope, meta.lifecycle and meta.revision. A Reference target is checked with ArtifactIds only when its type is an artifact type; external targets are allowed; only the parent must be an artifact id. readWithHistory adds the change log and feedback (already filed as an sc2 methodAdd). The AMD codec refuses an unconverted flat amendment. The provenance ChangeLogEntry is renamed FileChangeEntry. The inventory detector adds appendFileSync, appendSidecarLine and an import-based store-write rule, and every existing appender it newly flags gets an entry.
pros: A retry after any boundary, including head replaced but clear failed, reuses the staged operation id and appends the same entry
Production writes cannot silently skip durable staging
The old readers move onto the one decoder without turning any caller asynchronous
Identity meta is owned by each kind's codec, so the existing anchor and path code keeps working over a stored head
cons: More surface: a journal port with pending, a shared decoder and a codec context
Edits gates.ts readers (thin delegation) and renames a type used by the build change log

alternativesConsidered.name: Same store with an optional journal and re-derived operation id
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: As a1 but the journal is optional and the operation id is re-derived on every attempt.
alternativesConsidered.approach: ArtifactStore.write appends the log entry and replaces the head; a WriteJournal may be supplied; the operation id is recomputed from the prior revision and bytes each attempt; gates readers are left as they are.
cons: An absent journal leaves no durable pending content, so binding requirement 3 is not met in production
A retry after the head was replaced reads a new prior revision and derives a different operation id, so the log can hold two entries for one write
Leaves four independent JSON readers, which is the second reader the Story is meant to remove
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Smaller but fails binding requirement 3 and leaves the second reader.

alternativesConsidered.name: Store plus a real file-backed sidecar and journal inside s2
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: As a1 but s2 also implements the sidecar files, ordering and the durable pending head itself.
alternativesConsidered.approach: The a1 store with History over fixed file names beside each head, read-time filtering and de-duplication, and a durable pending-head file with replay at startup, all in s2.
pros: Works end to end in one Story
Crash recovery is testable with real files immediately
cons: Takes file layout, ordering, de-duplication and repair from s4, which owns sc5 and binding requirement 3
Fixes a line format s4 has not designed, so s4 would rewrite shipped code
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Complete but crosses into s4's boundary.

erDefinition.narrative: The common artifact model: an Artifact owns one Lifecycle (the shapes approved for the lifecycle Story), may bind to one tracker issue, and has references and attachments; its change log and feedback are separate sidecar records that carry the owning artifact id. A Task set holds Task artifacts, and a repository has one schema version.

Artifact.description: Any stored entity: an Epic, Story, Task, design document, plan, build or review record.

id.description: The artifact id from the s1 identity module.

description.description: A short human description; part of the content.

parent.description: The artifact this one derives from; the Epic, Story and Task chain is given by it.

references.description: Links to other artifacts or external things.

lifecycle.description: The one lifecycle of this artifact.

binding.description: The tracker issue this artifact is one to one with.

attachments.description: Supporting items attached to the artifact.

payload.description: The kind-specific content owned by its payload codec.

Lifecycle.description: Status, revision, approval, review, signoffs and staleness of one artifact; exactly one per artifact.

status.description: draft, pending-review, approved, in-signoff, changes-requested, signed-off, rejected, completed, withdrawn or superseded.

approval.description: The latest approval of a revision.

review.description: The latest review of a revision.

stale.description: Set when an upstream artifact moved on.

Revision.description: A content revision with the hash of the content it names and who made it.

contentHash.description: Hash of the canonical content, computed by the lifecycle rules.

override.description: The reason given when a blocking review was overridden.

Review.description: A review verdict on one revision.

Signoff.description: One signoff round on a revision.

request.description: The tracker comment or issue that asked for it.

Staleness.description: The record that an artifact was built on an upstream revision that has since changed.

TrackerBinding.description: The link to one tracker issue and what has been posted to it.

createdAtRevision.description: The revision current when the issue was created.

posted.description: What the framework posted to the issue.

pendingLink.description: A parent link not yet made.

Posting.description: One post to a tracker issue.

kind.description: milestone, task-list, design, review or plan.

externalId.description: The tracker's id for the post.

PendingLink.description: A parent and child link waiting to be made.

Attachment.description: A supporting artifact attached to the issue of the unit it describes.

externalId.description: The tracker's id for the attachment.

Reference.description: A typed link from one artifact to another or to an external thing.

entityId.description: The artifact id or external id linked to.

type.description: What kind of thing the target is.

fragment.description: A section or line range inside the target.

quote.description: A quoted passage from the target.

Actor.description: A person, agent or system that acts on an artifact; the id is namespaced by its source.

id.description: Namespaced id such as github:alice or insrc:daemon.

ChangeLogEntry.description: One append-only record of an operation on an artifact.

id.description: The operation id; the de-duplication key within the artifact.

operation.description: create, update, approve, review, complete and the others.

revision.description: The revision the operation produced or acted on.

addresses.description: The feedback entries this update addressed, or all.

Feedback.description: An immutable comment, suggestion or revision request on an artifact, with its replies.

anchor.description: The quote, its prefix and suffix, the section and the lines it was made on.

SidecarRecord.description: One line of a sidecar file: an entry and the id of the artifact that owns it.

changeLogEntry.description: Set on a change log line.

TaskSet.description: The Tasks file of a Story: the Task artifacts of its plan.

Task.description: One Task of a plan: an artifact with its own lifecycle and issue.

TaskPayload.description: The content of a Task artifact.

version.description: 1 is unconverted; 2 is the common model.
